About Me

Delivering real work for real clients

I study Business Management and Marketing at Nottingham Trent University. Through the Marketing Agency module I have worked on two live client campaigns, one for the Nottingham Safeguarding Adults Board and one for British Nordic Walking. I developing practical skills in campaign planning, strategic positioning, market research, and professional communication.

Alongside my studies I am part of the University Officer Training Corps, having completed a week-long rock climbing expedition in Wales, field exercise weekends, and weekly training throughout the year. The skills built through these commitments are communication, leadership, and performing reliably under pressure which are directly transferable to any professional environment.

This portfolio captures the evidence of my development and the quality of work I am capable of producing.

Teamwork

Worked across two client campaigns with external organisations, taking on defined responsibilities and contributing meaningfully to group outcomes.

Communication

Presented to the Nottingham Safeguarding Adults Board, adapting campaign messaging for a professional non-marketing audience.

Transferable Skills

Experience across client work, outdoor leadership, and service environments has built skills applicable across a wide range of industries and graduate roles.

Module Reflection

My journey through the module

February 2026 — Start of Module

"Starting this module I wasn't entirely sure what to expect and I was a bit uncertain. If I'm honest, marketing wasn't something I'd always been passionate about but I figured there was no better place to give it a go than this module and potentially change my mind. When I reflected on my values of being adventurous, having courage, and caring about the environment, I realised those aren't separate from a professional career, they're the foundation of one. This module pushed me to connect who I actually am to the skills I needed to build. That's where my PDP came from."

Week 4 — First Client Briefing

"By week 4 I was working on my first real client brief with people I'd only just met. I'd describe how I felt that day in three words, excited, motivated, and challenged. My confidence on understanding the brief was about 7 out of 10. The client had a clear awareness problem and limited marketing presence, which actually made the challenge feel manageable and interesting. What stood out was how naturally the group worked together, we structured the PowerPoint, delegated roles, and got a strong start without any friction. That was the first time I felt like I was actually working professionally rather than just studying."

May 2026 — End of Module

"Finishing this module I feel genuinely glad I did it. It wasn't always comfortable, especially with real client work with real deadlines being a a different pressure to standard assignments. But that discomfort is where the development happened. I've built skills in campaign planning, content strategy, collaboration and presentation that I'll carry into whatever career I end up in, not just marketing. The biggest shift for me wasn't a skill, it was a mindset. I came in not knowing what I wanted. I'm leaving with a portfolio, real evidence of what I can do, and a clearer sense of what I'm capable of."

Featured Projects

Live client work

Campaign · Community · Awareness

Nottingham Safeguarding Adults Board

Developed a one-week public awareness campaign for the Nottingham Safeguarding Adults Board as part of National Safeguarding Adults Week. The campaign focused on increasing awareness and improving access to safeguarding support, with particular attention given to underrepresented South Asian communities. Research into community spaces including Punjabi Forest directly informed the targeting strategy. Presented to the Board at the close of the project.

My Role

  • Contributed to campaign planning and idea development
  • Researched target audience and underrepresented communities including Punjabi Forest
  • Developed campaign messaging and tone of voice
  • Refined and improved presentation slides
  • Delivered final presentation to the Nottingham Safeguarding Adults Board

Skills Demonstrated

Campaign Development & Planning Market Research & Audience Analysis Collaboration & Working with Others Communication — Verbal & Written Presentation & Public Speaking
Strategy · Brand · Positioning

British Nordic Walking

Developed a strategic marketing approach for British Nordic Walking with emphasis on brand positioning and improving engagement across different audience segments. The work involved analysing BNW's current positioning, identifying competitive differences against WALX, and proposing a structured 6-month engagement strategy across community, GP, and university channels.

Key Contributions

  • Developed brand positioning comparison between BNW and WALX
  • Contributed to defining a clear strategic direction
  • Created a structured 6-month campaign timeline
  • Proposed multi-channel engagement strategies across community, GP and university sectors
  • Supported presentation delivery

Skills Demonstrated

Market Research & Audience Analysis Campaign Development & Planning Communication — Verbal & Written Collaboration & Working with Others Content Creation — Written & Visual
